nodes.label: MCP-RO-ARCH-001: read-only MCP connectors
nodes.rationale: A read only succeeds after: local tool allowlist, JSON-Schema argument validation, remote schema SHA-256 hash check, server-side binding of sensitive identifiers, bounded MCP call, provenance normalization, then audit — audit is fail-closed, required before the call, never logs payload/JQL/CQL/bearer.

nodes.label: Figma catalogue block -> REST API switch
nodes.rationale: Figma's remote MCP server only admits catalogue-listed clients (403 on dynamic registration); switching to the public REST API at api.figma.com kept every transport invariant intact (HTTPS, public address, port 443) while self-hosting an internal MCP server would have been indistinguishable from SSRF inside Docker.

nodes.label: Groq LLM provider adapter
nodes.rationale: Chosen for free-tier volume, high throughput, and an OpenAI-compatible API so one adapter covers Groq and OpenAI; model qwen/qwen3.6-27b is capped at 16384 output tokens and is a preview model with no availability guarantee; endpoint is pinned in code, never configurable, so a modified env file can't exfiltrate the API key to another host.

nodes.label: AgentReadWorkflow orchestration loop
nodes.rationale: The model's tool catalogue is derived only from public registry schemas and every proposed call is re-authorized by MCPReadWorkflow, so removing this module widens nothing; recoverable refusals return to the model as observations, everything else halts the loop by default rather than being silently worked around.
